title: DataAccessV1dot20
description: K-05 v1.20, a minor version of the data-access calls (T-1187: the sign-up reading only at a business with no live owner; T-1184's security note a, README open gap 46; DL-370, DL-999). It only adds to v1.19 (data-access.v1.19.schema.json, frozen and unchanged, referred to here, which refers on to every earlier version down to v1): every v1.19 definition is here under its own name, by reference, and none changes but the four it restates, each taking only a new optional field or a new refusal, so every v1 to v1.19 exchange is a v1.20 exchange. It adds no database call and changes no read: readOutboxRow reads as v1.3 to v1.13 say and readBusinessOwner as v1.4 says. Restated: rowReader.request (the optional businessOwner, whether the row's business has a live owner role, as v1.4's readBusinessOwner answers it), noReaderError (why gains businessHasOwner), rowReader.errors and rowReader.exchange (README item 80: with businessOwner live, a person with no role is never read by the sign-up line; without the field the exchange is v1.19's). Added: businessOwnerState, and rowReader.ownerExchange, rowReader.exchange narrowed to a request that states the field wherever the outcome reads it, the definition the v1.20 fixtures are listed under and a v1.20 consumer's mapping is checked by. Not model-facing, so number and length limits are schema rules here. Owner: the architect.

businessOwnerState.title: BusinessOwnerState
businessOwnerState.description: Whether the business a row was committed under has a live owner role (K-04 v1 person_roles: role owner, ended_at null), as v1.4's readBusinessOwner answers it for that business at the row's read (README item 80; T-1184's security note a; README open gap 46): live, the read answers an owner (its one live owner role's person) or moreThanOneOwner (two or more live owner roles: still a business that has an owner, README default 184); none, the read answers owner null, or the row has no business, which has no owner and is never read (README defaults 185 and 186). Never a third value: a read that fails (notFound, transient) gives no state, so no request is built and the row is refused before a reader is looked for (README default 188). It names no person, role or handle: the mapping reads only whether an owner exists (README default 190). New in v1.20.

rowReader.request.title: RowReaderRequest
rowReader.request.description: What the reader mapping reads (README items 44 and 80): v1.5's seven fields, each by reference to v1.5's own definition of it, which v1.6 to v1.19 keep unchanged, and v1.20's optional businessOwner, whether the row's business has a live owner role. Restated in v1.20 only to take it, so without the field the request is v1.19's. Not a database call: the seven come from readOutboxRow's answer and the row's bundle, as v1.5 says, and businessOwner from v1.4's readBusinessOwner for the row's business. Changed in v1.20.

businessOwner.description: Whether the row's business, the one readOutboxRow read the row under (the call's own: v1.3 readOutboxRow.request businessId), has a live owner role, read through v1.4's readBusinessOwner for that business at this mapping, on the primary, every time: by compose input and by finalize each, never taken from the turn's party read (v1.11 item 52), a cache or the Tool API's caller (README item 80, default 189). live: a person with no role is never read by the sign-up line there (noReader, businessHasOwner). none: item 44 reads as v1.5 says. Stated wherever the outcome reads it, a recipient who is a person, holds no role and is on a section 1 step (rowReader.ownerExchange requires it there); elsewhere it may be left out, and the consumer need not make the read. Left out everywhere: the request is v1.19's, and the mapping v1.5's. New in v1.20.

noReaderError.title: NoReaderError
noReaderError.description: No one reads the row, so compose input and finalize refuse it, and nothing is composed or sent (README items 44 and 80). why: noRole, lineHasNoReader and roleReadsAsNoOne as v1.5 defines them, and v1.20's businessHasOwner: the recipient, a person, holds no role at the row's business, the row's step is in section 1 of its flow, and the business has a live owner role (the request's businessOwner live), so the sign-up reading does not apply there: a business that has an owner is never read as its owner by someone who holds no role at it (T-1184's security note a). Named after noRole and before lineHasNoReader (README default 187); answered only to a request that states businessOwner live, so a v1.19 consumer never meets it. error and outboxRowId are v1.5's own, by reference. Changed in v1.20.

rowReader.errors.title: RowReaderErrors
rowReader.errors.description: noReader, the mapping's one refusal, restated in v1.20 to refer to v1.20's noReaderError. A row whose line is null, one whose step the row's bundle does not hold, and one whose owner read failed are refused before a reader is looked for (README item 35's table; default 188), and a read's own errors are that read's, not this mapping's. Changed in v1.20.

rowReader.exchange.title: RowReaderExchange
rowReader.exchange.description: README items 44 and 80, the consumers' reader mapping, as one exchange so its fixtures check it: not a database call. Restated in v1.20 to refer to v1.20's rowReader.request and rowReader.errors and to hold a request that states businessOwner live to item 80. call and given are v1.5's own, by reference. Its rules (dependentSchemas, on outcome), by number: 0 to 2 are v1.5's own, by reference (a recipient who holds a role is read by it, never by the line; a row with no person is noRole; a recipient with no role outside section 1 is noRole), and hold whatever businessOwner says; 3 to 6 are v1.5's rules 3 to 6 (the sign-up line's reader for a line to owner, staff or cust; lineHasNoReader for a line to no reader), each applying only while businessOwner is not live, with v1.5's own then by reference; 7 is new: a person with no role on a section 1 step at a business with a live owner is noReader, businessHasOwner, whatever the line. So without the field the exchange is v1.19's, and every v1.5 to v1.19 exchange passes. Changed in v1.20.

outcome.description: README item 44's rules with item 80's, each tying the outcome to the request. Together they decide every recipient with no role, and leave a recipient with a role to v1.3's mapping by role.

allOf.description: v1.5's rule 3, while the business has no live owner (businessOwner none, or left out as in v1.19): a person with no role, on a section 1 step whose line goes to the owner, is read as the owner, by the sign-up line (row-reader-s1-02-no-role-no-owner).
v1.5's rule 4, while the business has no live owner: a person with no role, on a section 1 step whose line goes to staff, is read as staff, by the sign-up line.
v1.5's rule 5, while the business has no live owner: a person with no role, on a section 1 step whose line goes to the customer (lane cust), is read as the customer, by the sign-up line.

v1.5's rule 6, while the business has no live owner: a person with no role, on a section 1 step whose line goes to no reader lane or cannot be told without a role (lineTo null), is noReader, lineHasNoReader (README default 62).

New in v1.20 (README item 80): a person with no role, on a section 1 step, at a business that has a live owner role (businessOwner live), is noReader, businessHasOwner, whatever lane the line goes to: the sign-up reading never applies at a business that has an owner (row-reader-s1-02-sam-after-hand-over; refuse-row-reader-sign-up-line-at-owned-business).

rowReader.ownerExchange.title: RowReaderOwnerExchange
rowReader.ownerExchange.description: The exchange of a v1.20 mapping: rowReader.exchange narrowed by allOf so that the request states businessOwner wherever the outcome reads it, a recipient who is a person, holds no role and is on a section 1 step (README item 80), as commitTurn.handleIdExchange narrows commitTurn.exchange (README 'v1.17'). Here a reader by the sign-up line always stands on a stated businessOwner none, and a missing or null state is refused (refuse-row-reader-owner-state-left-out, refuse-row-reader-owner-state-null): a consumer that did not read the owner never reads the row by the line. Every other request may leave the field out, since its outcome does not read it. The v1.20 fixtures are listed under this definition, and it is the definition a v1.20 consumer's mapping is checked against (T-1497, the row binding's port). New in v1.20.
